Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC task-f2ec14fd

## Learned rule
The input is a rectangular field divided into regions by full-length separator lines of a single color. Recolor every complete uniform separator row and complete uniform separator column from its original color to a new color; leave every other cell unchanged. The new separator color is 2 in the observed examples.

### Evidence from demo
Demo input was 23x30, with background 0 and pattern color 6. Full horizontal separator rows at indices 3 and 22 (0-based), and full vertical separators at columns 6, 28, and 29, were changed to 2 in the output. Other cells remained exactly as input.

### Evidence from solved test
Test input was 14x24 with color 1 forming full separator lines. Full horizontal rows 2, 6, and 9, plus full vertical columns 2, 15, 17, 18, 21, and 23 (0-based), were recolored to 2; all non-separator cells were preserved. Submission was confirmed CORRECT.

## Recognition procedure for recurrence
1. Identify rows and columns that are constant across their entire length/height and are part of the divider lattice (in examples, full lines of color 1 in the test, or full lines of color 0 amid a 0/6 pattern in demo).
2. Change every such separator line to color 2, including intersections.
3. Preserve all other cells exactly; do not recolor partial occurrences of the same color.
4. Output same grid dimensions.
